summary: Frontend-only regression + verification of 3 new global behaviours (scroll reveal on non-home pages, page fade transition, gold gradient CTA hover) plus reduced-motion + responsive + admin regression. All checks passed with zero console errors.

scroll_reveal_non_home.detail: First main>section on every page starts at opacity 1 (above-fold auto is-in). After gradual scroll to bottom, every section ended at opacity ~1 (0 stuck). Sections per page: /sell=3, /lettings=6, /landlords=5, /property-management=4, /investment=4, /mortgages=4, /contact=2.

homepage_excluded.result: Homepage correctly skipped by ScrollReveal; all 6 sections visible.

page_fade_transition.result: Route change /sell -> /landlords triggers .page-fade animation from 0 to 1 in ~0.5s. No permanent hidden state.

gold_gradient_cta_hover.result: Gold->amber gradient shifts, lift and glow apply on hover as designed.

reduced_motion.result: prefers-reduced-motion:reduce -> sections instantly visible, CTA transition disabled.

critical_code_review_comments: ScrollReveal.tsx: cleanup function returned from inside setTimeout is never used by React (useEffect cleanup only sees the outer clearTimeout). IntersectionObserver is not disconnected on unmount. Minor memory leak on client-side route changes; recommend hoisting the io reference to the outer effect scope and disconnecting in the effect cleanup.

RouteTransition.tsx: using key={pathname} unmounts/remounts the entire tree on every navigation which loses component state (form inputs, scroll positions inside components). Acceptable for marketing pages but risky if applied around stateful areas like /backoffice or /admin. Consider scoping RouteTransition to public marketing routes only.

globals.css: `.reveal{opacity:0}` combined with a 60ms setTimeout in ScrollReveal means for a very brief instant sections have no class and are visible, then flash to opacity:0 before is-in is added on above-fold. Not observed as visible flash in tests but consider adding `.reveal{opacity:0}` only via JS to eliminate risk on slow devices.

Selector `a.bg-[#D4AF37],button.bg-[#D4AF37]` is fragile — any refactor of the Tailwind arbitrary color class breaks the gold gradient globally. Prefer a semantic class (e.g. .cta-gold) applied to CTAs.
